text:
Not everyone agrees. The evidence is mixed, and a board member who knows the literature could undercut a memo that claims consensus. The strongest defensible version is that fully remote work hurts some kinds of work, not that remote work kills productivity.

- **Randomized evidence shows losses for fully remote work on some tasks.** Atkin, Schoar and Shinde (2023) found fully remote data-entry workers about 18% less productive than in-office peers. Gibbs, Mengel and Siemroth (2023) found output per hour fell at an IT firm after the move to remote work.
- **Collaboration and mentoring degrade.** Yang et al. (Nature Human Behaviour, 2022) found Microsoft's collaboration networks became more siloed under remote work. Emanuel, Harrington and Pallais (2023) found junior engineers got less feedback when not co-located.
- **Remote communication reduces creative output.** Brucks and Levav (Nature, 2022) found video-based teams generated fewer creative ideas than in-person teams.

Cite these as "fully remote work carries measurable costs for junior staff, collaboration, and creative tasks," not as proof that remote work reduces productivity generally. Bloom et al. (Nature, 2024) randomized hybrid work at Trip.com and found no productivity effect and about 33% lower attrition. Bloom's earlier call-center study found a 13% gain from working at home. A memo advocating return-to-office is better framed around hybrid versus fully remote, and around role type, than around a blanket claim. I haven't re-verified the exact figures against the papers, so check them before they go in the memo.
